content: The Heinrich Heine University of Düsseldorf, located in Düsseldorf, Germany, is named after the renowned German poet and political thinker Heinrich Heine, who was born in the city in 1797. Since its establishment as a full university in 1965, it has grown to include faculties of law, medicine, philosophy, mathematics and natural sciences, and economics. The university currently enrolls over 18,000 students, and its rector is Prof. Dr. Dr. Alfons Labisch, M.A. (Soz.). In 1806, Joachim Murat, Napoleon Bonaparte's brother-in-law and the ruler of the Duchy of Berg, expressed a desire to establish a university in Düsseldorf. At that time, only a few institutions resembling colleges existed, having developed between the 16th and 18th centuries. On December 12, 1811, Napoleon issued a decree to establish a university with five faculties in the duchy. However, the French invasion of Russia disrupted these plans, and the university was not founded at that time. In 1907, a medical academy was established in Düsseldorf, which began training students in 1923. In 1962, the state of North Rhine-Westphalia assumed responsibility for the academy from the city of Düsseldorf. Subsequently, in 1965, the state government decided to transform the medical academy into a university. On January 1, 1966, the university was officially constituted with a faculty of medicine and a combined faculty for natural sciences and philosophy. The opening ceremony took place on February 14, 1966. The central campus, located in the southern part of Düsseldorf, was completed in the 1970s, and its architectural style reflects the era of its construction. Initially, the university was not named after Heinrich Heine due to longstanding controversies. Heine was considered an unsuitable figurehead for both pragmatic and political reasons. It was not until December 20, 1988, that the university's senate decided to honor Düsseldorf's most famous son by naming the institution after him. The university has awarded honorary degrees to notable individuals, including Johannes Rau, former President of the Federal Republic of Germany; Paul Spiegel, former President of the Central Council of Jews in Germany; and Marcel Reich-Ranicki, a prominent literary critic. Heinrich Heine University maintains partnerships with several prestigious institutions worldwide, including the University of Nantes (France), the University of Naples Federico II (Italy), Peking University (China), the University of Alicante (Spain), the University of Reading (UK), the University of California, Davis (USA), Pennsylvania State University (USA), Charles University in Prague (Czech Republic), and Keio University in Tokyo (Japan). Additionally, the university participates in numerous SOCRATES/ERASMUS partnerships. The university offers a wide range of academic disciplines, including medicine, dental medicine, law, philosophy, German language and literature, Latin and Ancient Greek, English language and literature, Romance languages and literature (French, Spanish, Italian, Catalan), history, information science, medieval and Renaissance studies, Jewish studies, cultural and media studies, sports, journalism, linguistics and computational linguistics, modern Japanese studies, art history, social sciences and politics, mathematics, physics, chemistry, geography, biology, computer science, pharmacology, psychology, economics, and applied chemistry in economics.
